To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) English speakers without Mandarin training have difficulty discriminating tones and vowels; 2) experience in Mandarin improves the ability of English speakers to discriminate tones; 3) the ability to discriminate tones is not improved to the same extent as the ability to discriminate vowels; and 4) the T2-T4 contrast is difficult to learn for English speakers, and may be an inherent difficulty.

1) the discrimination accuracy of English speakers for Mandarin vowels and tones varies with their Mandarin learning experience and the type of sounds; 2) non-native language speakers are more sensitive to vowels than tones; 3) Mandarin vowels are easier for non-native speakers to learn and discriminate than Mandarin tones; 4) English speakers are able to learn Mandarin tones with training; 5) T2-T3 is a difficult tonal contrast for English speakers and may be inherently resistant to improvement.

1) the discrimination of Mandarin tones and vowels is differentially affected by native language experience, 2) English speakers with no Mandarin experience discriminate vowels more accurately than tones, while Mandarin learners are able to discriminate tones as accurately as Mandarin vowels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perception of Mandarin tones and vowels by native speakers of English.
the perception of Mandarin vowels and the tones by English speakers with varying Mandarin experience.
the perception of nonnative vowels and tones, and the effect of native language and experience in the second language on the perception of these sounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-native language speakers are less accurate in perceiving tonal distinction, but with enough experience in Mandarin they can discriminate some tones as well as vowels.
the difficulty of a contrast depends on both the native language and the type of sound.

the difficulty of Mandarin vowels and tonal contrasts for English speakers is not simply due to the similarity of these sounds to those in English, as the results showed that the two groups with varying Mandarin experience were able to discriminate the vowel contrasts and some of the tone contrasts as well as the English speakers with no experience in Mandarin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perception of Mandarin tones is not only affected by the native language experience, but also by the tonal structure of the language.

Mandarin vowels are easier to discriminate for English speakers at all stages, and that Mandarin tones are difficult for English speakers to perceive, but that experience in Mandarin may help improve their discrimination of tones.
the perception of nonnative sounds is a dynamic process that is affected by multiple factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the difficulty of a contrast is not necessarily related to its assimilation in the native language.
the relative difficulty of Mandarin vowel and tone perception for English speakers varies across contrasts and learning stages.
the difficulty in discriminating Mandarin tones may not only stem from their tonal status, but may be due to their phonological and phonetic characteristics as well.
